data.narrative:
Specter is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $6.8M to date. The comparable universe includes 9 private peers (Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI among them) and 1 public comparable, though the narrow peer set lacks sufficient density for robust multiples-based valuation.

Given data constraints, Stage-Progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($6.8M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $17M. This single-method triangulation necessarily limits precision; the Peer-Median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum threshold requirements (fewer than 3 datapoints in tightly-filtered cohorts).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $14M to $20M, centered on $17M. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct comparable transactions at identical stage and capital level, reliance on a single methodological input, and the nascent nature of the robotics sector's valuation precedents. Any forward valuation should be treated as provisional and revisited upon addition of material operational data (revenue, customer traction, or financing milestone) or identification of additional narrow-universe peers.
